notes: The shelf's namesake, and the tape the whole lore idea started from.
**It is a school assignment and it is cheerful the whole way down.**
Everything about the subject invites grief and the tape refuses it:
there is no anger, nothing rehearsed, and no mention of what was done
to him. It is a first-year cadet who got genuinely interested in his
own homework and wants to show his working. The sadness is entirely
the viewer's, and it arrives about four lines after the kid has
cheerfully moved on -- which costs the writing nothing to produce and
is the reason this tape works at all.
"School assignment" and "the author was in Starfleet" resolve to the
**Academy**: a heritage seminar, year one, which is also why a
twenty-year-old is addressing a dead ancestor down a lens. The brief
title: Dear Grandpa Tuvix
subtitle: Starfleet Academy heritage seminar, assignment four
author: first-year cadet, name withheld
extra: Dubbed from a friend's copy. He got an A minus.

lines.text: STARFLEET ACADEMY: HERITAGE SEMINAR, YEAR ONE
ASSIGNMENT FOUR: ADDRESS IT TO THEM
A friend sent me this one. I have watched it a lot.
Hi. Okay. This is for my heritage assignment.
We had to pick an ancestor and talk to them. So.
Dear Grandpa Tuvix. That still sounds strange.
He is reading off a padd and keeps losing his place.
I did the research first. The research was the fun part.
You go back up the maternal line and it is all names.
Names, postings, transfer dates. Hundreds of them.
And then there is you, and you are not a name.
You're listed as a species. Population: one.
I sat there for an hour. Then I changed my subject.
WHAT I FOUND
Grandma was Betazoid. Lower decks. Voyager.
Ensign. Sensor maintenance. Nobody writes about her.
She was aboard for all eighteen of your days.
The service record says almost nothing. Her letters do.
She said you were the easiest person on that ship.
Seven years from home, and you were easy to be near.
Off camera, somebody tells him to sit up straight.
So then: my mother. Talaxian, Vulcan and Betazoid.
Three ways at once, which the databases hate.
She walks into a room and the room settles down.
Telepath. Strong enough that we mention it like height.
She never joined up. She says the galaxy came to her.
I joined up. She thinks that is very funny.
It is a small galaxy. I want to be clear about that.
My closest friend here is Tuvok's great-granddaughter.
Yes. That Tuvok. I know. I know.
We worked it out in the mess hall, on a padd.
Twenty minutes and a great many arrows.
Her family, my family, and you in the middle of it.
Half of you was her great-grandfather. So we did the sums.
We are cousins. Sort of. There is no form for that.
She says that makes us complicated.
I said that's fine by me.
CONCLUSION
My instructor wants a thesis. Okay. Thesis.
You were around for eighteen days and there's still more of you.
There are nine of us now. We all laugh the same way.
He has clearly practised this. He is still nervous.
I would have liked you. I think you'd have liked us.
Anyway. That is the assignment. Thanks, Grandpa Tuvix.
END OF SUBMISSION. GRADE WITHHELD PENDING CITATIONS.
He got the A minus on appeal. He has never let it go.
